name: NAEOTOM Alpha clinical photon-counting CT
description: Siemens introduced a general-purpose dual-source X-ray CT scanner with two direct-conversion cadmium telluride photon-counting detector arrays. The arrays register individual X-ray interactions and distinguish energy bands for spectral imaging.

date.basis: Mayo Clinic gives April 2021 as the investigational installation month.

events.statement: Mayo Clinic installed a NAEOTOM Alpha as an investigational prototype in Rochester, Minnesota.

evidence.supports: Identifies the installed Alpha and its April 2021 investigational status.

date.basis: Date on the FDA determination letter.

events.statement: The U.S. FDA cleared NAEOTOM Alpha through the 510(k) process.

evidence.supports: Names NAEOTOM Alpha and dates the clearance.

date.basis: Date of the maker's launch announcement.

events.statement: Siemens Healthineers formally launched NAEOTOM Alpha in an announcement describing U.S. and European clearance and prior installations.

evidence.supports: Announces the launch and distinguishes cleared markets from the previous installations.

date.label: After FDA clearance in 2021
date.basis: Mayo reports clinical use beginning in 2021 after the FDA letter dated 30 September. These dates bound the start of use.

events.statement: Mayo Clinic began clinical use of the Alpha after the U.S. FDA clearance.
events.caveats: The first clinical day is unresolved. The stated year and clearance order do not settle the sequence relative to the public November launch.

evidence.supports: Dates the beginning of actual clinical use to 2021.
Identifies the installed model as Alpha and reports its transition into clinical service.

earliest_record.rationale: Mayo’s documented investigational installation predates clearance, formal launch and the documented start of clinical use.

links.statement: NAEOTOM Alpha builds on the SOMATOM Force dual-source configuration, exchanging its two conventional ceramic detector arrays for two cadmium telluride photon-counting arrays.
links.scope: Two-source scanner configuration carried forward from Force, with a different detector technology.

evidence.supports: Explicitly describes engineering continuity and replacement of detector arrays.

evidence.locator: Materials and Methods, First Clinical PCD CT system
evidence.supports: Separately characterizes dual-source operation and detector placement on the Alpha and energy-integrating Force systems.
Duke operators independently corroborate the detector change and shared detector coverage.

unresolved.note: Mayo names Count, Count Plus and Alpha as consecutive research generations. Component-level transfers from the CounT prototypes into Alpha are unresolved.
